text:
Mitch Marner's second season in Vegas looks a lot like his years in Toronto: the puck finds teammates. He has 18 points in 16 games, ran a point streak to ten games early this month, and 13 of his points over his last ten games were assists. He played 657 games for his hometown Maple Leafs before signing with the Golden Knights, and Toronto's search for a replacement is still a headline topic.

The odd part is the goals. He has two on 4.19 expected, shooting 5.3 percent against a career-level range near 13. He keeps getting the looks, and goals tend to follow chances; a hot week would not surprise us. His on-ice results are close to what the chances say, so this is not a lucky line padding his totals.

Evolving-Hockey had him 16th among 401 forwards last season at 2.9 wins above replacement, mostly from even-strength offense. Our projection lands around 81 points, with about 20 goals. If you are watching Vegas, watch Marner on the half wall with the puck, and then watch who scores.
headline: Marner's ten-game point streak, mostly assists
